problem: allow() now unconditionally appends `now` to the per-key queue even when the request is denied, so a retrying client perpetually refills its own window and is never re-admitted, while the queue grows proportional to request rate instead of staying capped near `limit`.
suggested_fix: Only append `now` to the queue when `allowed` is True (restore the original `if allowed: q.append(now)` gate), which re-caps the queue at `limit` and lets denied clients recover once earlier accepted timestamps age out of the window.

problem: The field `self._accepted` and `_in_window` assume only accepted requests are stored, but nothing in the code enforces that invariant, so this bug (or one like it) is easy to silently reintroduce.
suggested_fix: Add a one-line comment above `allow()` stating the invariant that only accepted requests are recorded in `self._accepted`.
